newsitem.title: USA: KKR reaps huge profit from Duracell sale.
newsitem.headline: KKR reaps huge profit from Duracell sale.

text.p: Leveraged buy-out specialist Kohlberg Kravis & Roberts Co (KKR) has turned an initial $350 million investment into more than $3 billion with the sale of Duracell International Inc to Gillette Co, a KKR spokeswoman said.

The savvy Wall Street firm bought Duracell in 1988 and was able to reap the huge profit through an initial public offering and three secondary offerings that transformed the investment into $1.2 billion.

Furthermore, KKR still holds a $2 billion stake in Duracell following Thursday's $7 billion acquisition by Gillette, bringing the investment firm's total profit to some $3.2 billion, the spokeswoman said.
The huge reward came one day after KKR called off its $2.7 billion planned acquisition of five Talegen insurance units from Xerox Corp.

The Duracell transaction marks the second time in the past month that KKR pulled in a huge profit through the sale of its holdings. It agreed in August to sell its 64 percent stake in American Re Corp to Munich Reinsurance Co for $3.3 billion, bringing the firm an aggregrate return of about $2 billion from its initial $300 million investment.
